- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% downward adjustment to 30d forecast mean.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.50), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average if no clear trend.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast growth rate by 0.2–0.5% per event to account for supply pressure.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model tends to overcorrect; apply smoothing filter to avoid abrupt upward revisions.
